topic: What interference management strategies are critical when scaling terminal density for rainfall estimation in shared spectrum environments?
consensus_response: When scaling terminal density for rainfall estimation in shared spectrum environments, adaptive resource allocation strategies and Hybrid Beamforming (HBF) techniques are crucial to mitigate rain-induced fading and polarization effects. The increased path loss due to rain-induced attenuation reduces signal strength, increasing interference between adjacent terminals. Strong polarization correlation exacerbates this issue. HBF can adaptively adjust transmission beams to mitigate these effects, while adaptive resource allocation strategies dynamically adjust transmission power and frequency assignment based on real-time channel conditions. Machine Learning (ML) assisted interference management can also predict rain-induced fading by analyzing historical data and real-time sensor readings, further improving system reliability.
reference_context: Rainfall estimation in shared spectrum environments is affected by weather-induced impairments due to rain, with microwave signals experiencing attenuation at frequencies above 10 GHz. Rain measurements from different sources (rain gauge, radar, satellite) have strengths and drawbacks, highlighting the need for numerical models to integrate their strengths and address limitations.
